rationale: SUPERAGING is a feasibility protocol for a digital multidomain program in frail/prefrail Korean older adults. PD is an exclusion criterion; falls and pain are background/exercise language, not study symptom outcomes. Frozen pair: fresh sage and pain severity.

Real-world early experience program treating cervical dystonia with daxibotulinumtoxinA in 234 adults; clinical reason for treatment/retreatment and symptom relief are documented, but no standardized dystonia severity outcome is reported. Pain is only an injection-site adverse event, not pain severity of PD. Frozen pair: fresh sage and pain severity.

Case report of a 36-year-old woman with CMT2 and young-onset Parkinsonism; neurological examination documents rigidity with bradykinesia/rest tremor, but no standardized rigidity severity scale. No food exposure. Frozen pair: fresh sage and pain severity.

Post-hoc safety/efficacy analysis of 244 PD patients in a 52-week open-label foslevodopa/foscarbidopa infusion trial by prior DBS status; Table 2 reports falls as treatment-emergent adverse events (3/24 vs 37/220). This is adverse-event frequency, not a falls-prevention endpoint. Frozen pair: fresh sage and pain severity.

Two-patient rTMS case report for levodopa-induced dyskinesia in PD. Baseline rigidity is described and UPDRS Part III total is recorded, but separate rigidity results are absent; treatment-related injection/head/neck pain is not assessed, and no food exposure. Frozen pair: fresh sage and pain severity.
Results p. 772 describe increasing leg pain and discomfort in one of nine patients after 96 hours off levodopa. This is a medication-withdrawal symptom observation, without a fresh sage assignment.
